subject: Erdrick's Sword
text: The path to Erdrick's Sword in Charlock Castle is A, D, K, O, P, N, I, J, 2.

evidence.quote: Path to Erdrick's Sword:...A, D, K, O, P, N, I, J, 2

subject: DragonLord
text: The path to the Courtyard and DragonLord in Charlock Castle is A, D, K, O, R, S, *.

evidence.quote: Path to Courtyard/DragonLord:...A, D, K, O, R, S, *

subject: Stairways
text: Letters A through S and a through s mark stairways in Charlock Castle.

evidence.quote: A-S/a-s : Stairways *: This stairway takes you out to the Courtyard at Charlock.

subject: Stairway *
text: Stairway * leads to the Courtyard at Charlock, where you reach the DragonLord by going all the way left, then up, then right, then down.

evidence.quote:
*: This stairway takes you out to the Courtyard at Charlock. You can see the wiley DragonLord
   when you first enter; however, to get to him, go all the way left, then up, then right, then
   down, and you'll be there.

subject: Doors 1
text: Doors at 1 need a Magic Key to open, though stairways B and C do not lead anywhere useful.

evidence.quote:
1: Doors (need Magic Key to open; moot point cause you can't get anywhere useful through 
   stairways B and C)

subject: Chest 2
text: Chest 2 contains Erdrick's Sword, and otherwise is empty.

evidence.quote: 2: Chest; Contains Erdrick's Sword, otherwise is empty

subject: Barrier floors
text: Barrier floors drain hitpoints unless you have Erdrick's Armor.

evidence.quote:
/: Those wierd barrier floors that take out a crapload of hitpoints unless you have Erdrick's
   Armor

subject: Stairway T
text: On the sixth floor of Charlock Castle, the T stairway never ends, but walking back up the stairs once exits the loop.

evidence.quote:
*** On the sixth floor, the T stairway never ends; you could seriously keep going down forever
    and it'd never end. If you happen to go down here, just go up the stairway once and you'll
    be out of it.

subject: D-PAD
text: The D-PAD moves your character around and moves the cursor on menus.

evidence.quote: D-PAD: Move your character around, move cursor on menu

subject: A BUTTON
text: The A BUTTON selects a choice on the menu.

evidence.quote: A BUTTON: Select a choice on the menu

subject: B BUTTON
text: The B BUTTON de-selects or goes back in the menu.

evidence.quote: B BUTTON: De-Select/Go Back in the menu

subject: TALK
text: The TALK command allows you to talk to someone in front of you.

evidence.quote: TALK: Talk to someone in front of you

subject: STATUS
text: The STATUS command checks your fighter's status, including equipped equipment.

evidence.quote: STATUS: Check on your fighter's status, including equipped stuff

subject: STAIRS
text: The STAIRS command lets you go up or down stairs when standing on them.

evidence.quote: STAIRS: Go up/down stairs when youa re standing on them

subject: SEARCH
text: The SEARCH command searches the floor directly under you, revealing hidden items and chests.

evidence.quote: SEARCH: Search the floor/ground directly under you, revealing hidden items and chests

subject: SPELL
text: The SPELL command casts a spell, where some spells work only in battle and others only outside battle.

evidence.quote: SPELL: Cast a spell (some can only be cast in battle; some only when not it a battle)

subject: ITEM
text: The ITEM command is used to use an item.

evidence.quote: ITEM: Use an item

subject: DOOR
text: The DOOR command opens a door right in front of you.

evidence.quote: DOOR: Open a door right in front of you

subject: TAKE
text: The TAKE command takes the item revealed to you by searching.

evidence.quote: TAKE: Take the item that a search revealed to you

subject: ATTACK
text: The ATTACK battle command attacks the enemy you are fighting.

evidence.quote: ATTACK: Attack the enemy you are fighting

subject: RUN
text: The RUN battle command allows you to run away from an enemy.

evidence.quote: RUN: Run away from the enemy (don't be afraid to use this!)

subject: Name
text: As you travel about Alefgard, only the first four letters of your name will show.

evidence.quote:
Keep in mind that as you travel about Alefgard, only the
first four letters of your name will show.

subject: King's Treasure
text: The King allows you to take treasure consisting of 120 Gold (120-G), a torch, and a key.

evidence.quote:
The King allows you to take his treasure, which consists of 120 Gold (120-G), a torch, and
a key.

subject: King's Chamber Door
text: A guard explains how to open the door with a key, allowing you to open it and go down the stairs in the corner.

evidence.quote:
the other tells you
how to open a door (with a key). Well, open the door, and head down the stairs in the corner.

subject: Save Game
text: Guards outside the throne room tell you how to save your game, though you cannot save until you leave the castle.

evidence.quote:
The guards outside of the 
throne room will tell you how to save your game. You can't do it until you leave the castle, 
though.

subject: Brecconary
text: From the overworld outside Tantagel Castle, the small town of Brecconary lies to the east, where you may fight slimes.

evidence.quote:
Make a bee-line to
the small town to the east; if you get in a fight with a slime, go ahead and kill it.

subject: King Lorik
text: Townspeople in Brecconary advise seeing King Lorik after your experience level raises, that monsters get harder across bridges, and to watch out when crossing swamps.

evidence.quote:
See King Lorik after 
experience level raises; It gets harder after crossing bridges; and Watch out when crossing a 
swamp.

subject: Brecconary Townsfolk
text: Two men surrounded by stone in Brecconary tell you that you can buy keys somewhere and to come back if cursed.

evidence.quote:
the two guys 
surrounded by stone will tell you that you can buy keys somewhere and to come back if cursed.

subject: Brecconary Weapon Shop
text: At the weapon shop, you should buy a Club(60-G) and Clothes(20-G), leaving you with 40-G.

evidence.quote: Here, you should buy a Club(60-G) and the Clothes(20-G). This will leave you with 40-G.

subject: Leather Armor
text: Leather Armor(70-G) requires collecting 30-G, plus an emergency visit to the nearest inn(6-G) brings the target to 36-G.

evidence.quote:
Now, you have to make enough money to get the Leather Armor(70-G), which means you have to get 
30-G. Actually, you should always have enough to make an emergency visit to the nearest 
inn(6-G), so now you need to collect 36-G.

subject: Charlock Castle
text: Charlock Castle layout includes SURFACE, F1, F2, F3, and F4.
